issue_context.title: Broken index files can cause constraint violation on recreate
issue_context.body:
Not much detail on the issue, but it appears that the recreate function can break in some scenarios.

The underlying issue is that a block is registered in two different volumes, causing the `DuplicateBlock` to be filled. In some variation of the issue, it appears that there can be multiple such duplicates which causes an update to attempt to register the same block for the same volume twice in the table giving a constraint violation.

The most likely location of the error is here:
https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/blob/master/Duplicati/Library/Main/Database/LocalRecreateDatabase.cs#L685-L726
comments:
> The underlying issue is that a block is registered in two different volumes

Didn't this used to be (maybe still is?) normal if a block turns to waste then is needed again as a new block?
The index reflects the dblock, and the block is waste in one or more dblocks, but not waste for the new one.
Even if recycling blocks out of DeletedBlock was added recently (not sure), older code may leave duplicates.

My checker14.py script flags 11 of these, while the job database's DuplicateBlock table is completely empty.
Interestingly, recreate test only put two in DuplicatiBlock table, but point is that duplicates might be normal.

This issue has been mentioned on **Duplicati**. There might be relevant details there:

https://forum.duplicati.com/t/problem-after-update-to-2-1-0-2-beta/19788/20

Seems to still be a problem:
https://forum.duplicati.com/t/recreate-constraint-violation-on-duplicateblock/19927
